newsitem.title: UK: Higher oil price fuels BP profit.
newsitem.headline: Higher oil price fuels BP profit.

text.p: British Petroleum on Tuesday reported a 30 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 2.62 billion pounds ($4.28 billion), thanks to strong oil prices and higher production levels.

The result excludes a fourth quarter exceptional charge of 341 million pounds, representing one-off costs for restructuring related to the merger of BP and Mobil Corp's downstream operations in Europe.
BP said "targets are in place to keep underlying performance improving", adding there may be some oil price volatilty in coming months because of worldwide production growth.
BP said it expects its own oil production to increase further this year, while margins on selling fuel may improve if oil prices weaken later in the year.
But refining margins are likely to remain subdued with some volatility seen over the winter months due to low gasoil stock levels.
In chemicals, healthy demand should keep prices steady, but margins may suffer from high feedstock prices. Results will remain sensitive to the pound's strength, BP said.
